titel: The Prague Compacts with the Council of Basel (1433)
autor: The legates of the Council of Basel and the Bohemian and Moravian diet
quelle: Archiv český III (Prague 1844), section VI, Acts no. 4, 'První námluvy kompaktát' (Cedule A), pp. 398–403, Latin with the old Czech version in a parallel column. Read against the page images of three internet archive scans (archivesk01naukgoog, archivesk14nugoog, archiveskilista13naukgoog). English: the site's working translation.
hinweis: The first agreement on the Four Articles between the legates of the Council of Basel and the diet of Bohemia and Moravia, Prague, 30 November 1433, as printed by Palacký's Archiv český from several old manuscripts. It was revised at Brno in 1435 and proclaimed in its final form at Jihlava on 5 July 1436, with Sigismund received as king; that final form is not carried here. The Latin is carried in excerpts; omitted reasoning is marked [...]. The Czech column of the edition is not carried. All three scans are damaged in places (margins cut, letters blurred); the text was read across them.

sections.blurb: Peace and unity first; then the chalice granted to those who have the usage, public sins punished only by lawful courts, preaching only by approved priests, and the church's right to own towns and castles affirmed. The diet accepts and promises to press for reform.

units.orig: In nomine domini Jesu Christi. Haec, quae infra scripta sunt, per gratiam sancti spiritus concordata sunt inter legatos sacri generalis concilii Basiliensis et generalem congregationem inclyti regni Bohemiae et marchionatus Moraviae in civitate Pragensi:
units.en: In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. The things written below have been agreed, by the grace of the Holy Spirit, between the legates of the holy general Council of Basel and the general assembly of the renowned kingdom of Bohemia and margraviate of Moravia, in the city of Prague:
units.note: The Prague diet of St Martin, November 1433, after the Bohemian embassy, Prokop the Bald among them, had disputed the Four Articles at Basel that spring. The Czech column of the edition gives the year in full, 1433, in Prague.

units.titel: Peace and unity; the censures lifted
units.orig: 1. Primo, dicta congregatio nomine dictorum regni et marchionatus, et pro ipso regno et marchionatu, omnibusque ac singulis eorundem regni et marchionatus, qui sunt de parte ipsorum, recipient et acceptabunt et facient bonam, firmam et perpetuam pacem et ecclesiasticam unitatem, quam profitebuntur et firmabunt debito modo. 2. Quo facto dicti legati auctoritate dicti concilii admittent et recipient dictam pacem et unitatem, et pronuntiabunt pacem generalem universi populi Christiani cum incolis et habitatoribus dictorum regni et marchionatus, tollent omnes sententias censurae et plenariam abolitionem facient. Et mandabunt universis et singulis Christi fidelibus, quod nemo deinceps dictum regnum et marchionatum propter praeterita infamare praesumat, nec ipsos aut eorum incolas invadere vel offendere, sed cum eis Christianam pacem observent, ipsosque tamquam fratres eorum, sanctae videlicet matris ecclesiae filios reverentes et obedientes, habeant et fraterna dilectione contractent.
units.en: 1. First, the said assembly, in the name of the said kingdom and margraviate and for that kingdom and margraviate, and all and each of that kingdom and margraviate who are of their party, shall receive, accept and make a good, firm and perpetual peace and church unity, which they shall profess and confirm in due form. 2. This done, the said legates, by the authority of the said council, shall admit and receive that peace and unity, and shall proclaim a general peace of the whole Christian people with the inhabitants of the said kingdom and margraviate, shall lift all sentences of censure and make a full abolition. And they shall command all and each of Christ's faithful that no one shall henceforth presume to defame the said kingdom and margraviate because of the past, or to attack or harm them or their inhabitants, but that they keep Christian peace with them, and hold them as their brothers, that is, as reverent and obedient sons of holy mother church, and deal with them in brotherly love.
units.note: The first price of the chalice is 'church unity': the Bohemians submit to the church before anything is granted. In return every censure, the crusade bull's excommunications among them (Bull [1]), is lifted, and no one may 'defame Bohemia because of the past'. The opening letters of several lines are cut off in one scan and blurred in another; the text was read across all three.

units.orig: 3. Circa materiam primi articuli, quem ambasiatores dictorum regni et marchionatus obtulerunt sacro concilio sub hac forma: „quod communio divinissimae eucharistiae utilis et salubris sub utraque specie, scilicet panis et vini, universis Christi fidelibus in regno Boemiae et marchionatu Moraviae et locis eis in hac parte adhaerentium constitutis, per sacerdotes libere ministretur“, est hoc modo concordatum: quod dictis Bohemis et Moravis suscipientibus ecclesiasticam unitatem et pacem realiter cum effectu, et in omnibus aliis, quam in usu communionis utriusque speciei, fidei et ritui universalis ecclesiae conformibus, ille et illi, qui talem usum habent, communicabunt sub duplici specie cum auctoritate domini nostri Jesu Christi et ecclesiae, verae sponsae ejus; et articulus ille in sacro concilio discutietur ad plenum, [...] Et omnibus mature et digeste pertractatis, nihilominus si in desiderio habendi dictam communionem sub duplici specie perseveraverint, hoc eorum ambasiatoribus indicantibus, sacrum concilium sacerdotibus dictorum regni et marchionatus communicandi sub utraque specie populum, eas videlicet personas, quae in annis discretionis constitutae, reverenter et devote postulaverint, facultatem pro eorum utilitate et salute in domino largietur; hoc semper observato, quod sacerdotes sic communicantibus semper dicant, quod ipsi debent firmiter credere, quod non sub specie panis caro tantum, nec sub specie vini sanguis tantum, sed sub qualibet specie est integer totus Christus.
units.en: 3. On the matter of the first article, which the ambassadors of the said kingdom and margraviate presented to the holy council in this form: 'that the communion of the most divine eucharist, useful and salutary, be freely given by the priests in both kinds, that is of bread and wine, to all Christ's faithful in the kingdom of Bohemia and the margraviate of Moravia and in the places adhering to them in this matter', it has been agreed in this way: that to the said Bohemians and Moravians, who receive church unity and peace really and in effect, and who in all other things than the use of communion in both kinds conform to the faith and rite of the universal church, he and those who have that usage shall communicate in both kinds with the authority of our Lord Jesus Christ and of the church, his true bride; and that article shall be discussed fully in the holy council [...]. And when everything has been treated maturely and in order, if they nonetheless persevere in the desire to have the said communion in both kinds, and their ambassadors so declare, the holy council will grant the priests of the said kingdom and margraviate the faculty of giving communion in both kinds to the people, namely to those persons of the age of discretion who ask for it reverently and devoutly, for their benefit and salvation in the Lord; always provided that the priests always tell those who so communicate that they must firmly believe that not the flesh alone is under the species of bread, nor the blood alone under the species of wine, but the whole Christ entire is under each species.
units.note: The chalice is granted, but as a 'faculty' of the church to those 'who have that usage', not as a law of God for all: the council's words stand against the article's 'universis', to all the faithful. The omitted lines leave the question of whether the chalice is commanded by Christ to the council. The Domažlice song has the cardinal propose exactly this (Domažlice Rome [4]).

units.orig: 4. Legati sacri concilii per suas literas auctoritate sacri concilii mandabunt universis et singulis, cujuscunque status aut conditionis existant, ut dictis Bohemis et Moravis, utentibus dicta communione sub duplici specie, nemo audeat improperare, aut eorum famae aut honori detrahere; et hoc idem faciet sacrum concilium, quando concessionem libertationis faciet memoratam.
units.en: 4. The legates of the holy council shall by their letters, on the authority of the holy council, command all and each, of whatever status or condition, that no one dare reproach the said Bohemians and Moravians who use the said communion in both kinds, or detract from their good name or honour; and the holy council will do the same when it makes the said grant of freedom.
units.note: Twelve years after the crusade bull called them 'nurslings of iniquity' (Bull [1]), the council forbids anyone to reproach them.

units.orig: 6. Circa materiam de cohibitione et correptione peccatorum, in qua posuistis articulum sub his verbis: „omnia peccata mortalia, et praesertim publica, per eos, quorum interest, rationabiliter et secundum legem dei cohibeantur, corrigantur et eliminentur“, ecce verbum „per eos, quorum interest“, nimis est generale, et posset esse offendiculum; [...] Dicimus ergo, quod secundum scripturae sacrae sententiam, sanctorumque documenta doctorum, sic katholice est tenendum: quod omnia peccata mortalia, praesertim publica, quantum rationabiliter fieri potest, secundum legem dei et sanctorum patrum instituta sunt cohibenda, corripienda et eliminanda; potestas autem puniendi criminosos non ad privatas personas, sed ad eos tantummodo pertinet, qui jurisdictionem habent in eos fori, distinctione juris et justitiae ordine observatis.
units.en: 6. On the matter of the restraint and correction of sins, in which you set out the article in these words: 'that all mortal sins, and especially public ones, be restrained, corrected and rooted out reasonably and according to the law of God by those whose concern it is', see, the phrase 'by those whose concern it is' is too general and could be a stumbling block; [...] We say therefore that, according to the meaning of holy Scripture and the teachings of the holy doctors, it is to be held in the catholic way: that all mortal sins, especially public ones, are to be restrained, corrected and rooted out as far as can reasonably be done, according to the law of God and the institutions of the holy fathers; but the power to punish criminals belongs not to private persons, but only to those who have jurisdiction over them in the court, the distinction of law and the order of justice being observed.
units.note: The article is accepted; its executors are taken away. 'Those whose concern it is' had meant the brotherhoods themselves, with their punishments 'according to God's law', banishment, flogging, burning and drowning, of 'no person excepted' (Ordinance [12]). After 1433 only lawful courts may punish. The Latin addresses the Bohemians as 'you': these are the council's answers to their articles.

units.orig: 7. Circa materiam de praedicatione verbi dei, in qua posuistis articulum hoc tenore: „quod verbum dei a sacerdotibus domini et levitis idoneis libere ac fideliter predicetur“; ne ex verbo „libere“ sumeretur occasio vagae et dispendiosae libertatis, quam nec vos, ut saepe dixistis, intenditis, circumstantionandum est. Dicimus, quod secundum scripturae sacrae sententiam, sanctorumque documenta doctorum, sic katholice est tenendum: quod verbum dei a sacerdotibus domini et levitis ad hoc idoneis, et per superiores, ad quos pertinet, approbatis et missis, libere, non tamen passim, sed ordinate et fideliter praedicetur, salva auctoritate pontificis, qui est praeordinator in cunctis, juxta sanctorum patrum instituta.
units.en: 7. On the matter of the preaching of the word of God, in which you set out the article in this tenor: 'that the word of God be freely and faithfully preached by the priests of the Lord and suitable deacons', the word 'freely' must be qualified, so that no occasion be taken from it for a wandering and harmful liberty, which, as you have often said, you do not intend either. We say that, according to the meaning of holy Scripture and the teachings of the holy doctors, it is to be held in the catholic way: that the word of God is to be preached freely by the priests of the Lord and deacons suitable for it, approved and sent by the superiors to whom this belongs, not indiscriminately, however, but in order and faithfully, saving the authority of the bishop, who is the one who ordains in all things, according to the institutions of the holy fathers.
units.note: 'Freely, but not indiscriminately': the preachers of the field armies, priests who marched with the brotherhoods and preached in the market squares, now need a bishop's approval and mission.

units.titel: The fourth article: the church may own castles and towns
units.orig: 8. Circa materiam articuli ultimi, sub his verbis expressi: „non licet clero tempore legis gratiae super bonis temporalibus seculariter dominari“: meminimus, quod dum in sacro concilio super hoc disputatio ageretur publica et solemnis, ille, qui ad disputandum per sacrum concilium exstitit deputatus, duas conclusiones posuit sub hiis verbis: prima, quod clerici non religiosi, seu qui voto se ad hoc non obligaverunt, licite possunt habere et possidere quaecumque bona temporalia, hereditates paternas aut aliorum, si eis relinquantur, et alia bona juste acquisita ex causa donationis vel alterius liciti contractus vel arte licita; secunda, quod ecclesia potest licite habere et possidere bona temporalia, mobilia et immobilia, domos, praedia, villas, oppida, castra, civitates, et in eis habere privatum et civile dominium. Ille siquidem, qui ex vestris ambasiatoribus disputabat, concessit easdem, [...] Sed quoniam doctrina ecclesiae non est verbis ambiguis pertractanda, sed plane: propterea id, quod secundum legem dei et sanctorum documenta doctorum katholice censendum est, duximus exprimendum: videlicet praemissas duas conclusiones esse veras, quodque ecclesiastici viri bona ecclesiae, quorum sunt administratores, debent fideliter administrare, juxta sanctorum patrum salubria instituta, ipsaque bona ecclesiae ab aliis non debent injuste detineri vel occupari.
units.en: 8. On the matter of the last article, expressed in these words: 'it is not lawful for the clergy, in the time of the law of grace, to hold secular dominion over temporal goods': we remember that when a public and solemn disputation was held on this in the holy council, the man deputed by the holy council to dispute set out two conclusions in these words: first, that clerics who are not religious, or who have not bound themselves to this by a vow, may lawfully have and possess any temporal goods, inheritances from their fathers or others if these are left to them, and other goods justly acquired by gift or another lawful contract or by a lawful craft; second, that the church may lawfully have and possess temporal goods, movable and immovable, houses, estates, villages, towns, castles, cities, and have private and civil dominion in them. He who disputed for your ambassadors conceded them, [...] But since the church's teaching is not to be handled in ambiguous words but plainly, we have resolved to express what is to be held in the catholic way according to the law of God and the teachings of the holy doctors: namely, that the two conclusions set out above are true; and that churchmen ought to administer faithfully the goods of the church of which they are the administrators, according to the salutary institutions of the holy fathers; and that these goods of the church ought not to be unjustly withheld or occupied by others.
units.note: The fourth article is answered with its opposite. The church may own 'towns, castles, cities' with full dominion, and its goods 'ought not to be unjustly withheld or occupied by others': the lands the brotherhoods and lords had taken from churches and monasteries since 1420. This is the article the pope in the Domažlice song wanted passed over in silence (Domažlice Rome [5]). For the game it is the price of the early settlement.

units.orig: 9. Dicta vero congregatio declarationem dictorum trium articulorum, quae veritati sacrae scripturae innititur, suscipit et acceptat. Verum quia circa ipsorum trium articulorum materias nonnullis videtur abusus plures et deordinationes aliquas currere: est intentionis ipsius congregationis, quod super reformatione dictorum abusuum et deordinationum intendit in sacro concilio per suos ambasiatores instantiam et sollicitudinem adhibere;
units.en: 9. But the said assembly receives and accepts the declaration of the said three articles, which rests on the truth of holy Scripture. But since it seems to some that many abuses and some disorders are current in the matters of these three articles, it is the intention of the assembly to press and take care, through its ambassadors in the holy council, for the reform of these abuses and disorders;
units.note: The assembly accepts the declarations of the 'three articles', sin, preaching and property, and reserves the reform of the church's abuses for further negotiation. The Prague text was revised at Brno in 1435 and proclaimed with Sigismund's guarantees at Jihlava on 5 July 1436; that final form is not carried here.
